Same algorithm (n<7 insertion sort, presorted early return, med3 pivot for n>7, nine-element med3 for n>40, 3-way partition). A Python port of exactly that code (analysis/verify/agg_window_tie/pgqsort.py) reproduces every tie order I checked: (depname,salary) 7 9 11 10 8|5 2|3 4 1; (depname) 11 7 9 8 10|5 2|3 1 4; salary DESC 8 10 11 ...; x DESC NULLS FIRST 43 42 5 4 3 2 1; f_time DESC id 6 before 5; tenk1 unique1<10 sorted by four from heap order -> 0 8 4|5 9 1|6 2|3 7 (index-order input gives a different answer, so PG's input was heap order and Gres already scans in that order).

Gres evaluates calls independently in written order.

The base scan (exec.rs:17295 collect_cursor_bounded with read_ctx.blocking_query_memory), join output (join.rs:1085 push_bounded_join_row via JoinPolicy from subquery.rs:171), lateral cache (exec.rs:13815/13845) and count_join_rows (exec.rs:18391) honour the 20 MiB policy. Nine call sites ignore the knob and use the hard constant scanner.rs:939 (16 MiB): exec.rs:24253 key_source_rows (the ORDER BY sort path), exec.rs:24427 ensure_blocking_rows_fit, exec.rs:18505, srf.rs:2321 MemoryBudget, cte.rs:492, grouping.rs:496, setops.rs:353, agg.rs:2872, join.rs:57 JoinPolicy::default. That is why a full tenk1 base scan passes but `... FROM tenk1 ORDER BY x` fails while `... where hundred < 48 order by ...` (btree_index) passes.

Fix location 'JoinIndex must accept ctid keys so tenk1 ctid joins hash' is stale: join.rs:969 hashes_like_it_compares already lists `Datum::Tid(_)` (commit 0100c4401, 2026-08-15, before this CI run) with a comment naming tidscan's tenk1 self-joins. tidscan fails because exec.rs:19243 `if !wants_system_column(read_ctx.refs)` skips try_execute_local_join_count (18343) whenever ctid is referenced, so the join goes through build_from -> join_relations and materializes 10000 x 34-datum output rows (> 20 MiB) in push_bounded_join_row.

count_join_rows (join.rs:139) is listed as a firing site but it can only raise 53200 when right_match_bytes > budget (right/full joins), and it never returns an error for an oversized index (it just drops it, line 155-162). It is not where any of these statements fail.

Top-K pushdown never applies to these tables: exec.rs:18995 top_k_pushdown_for_select requires table.sharded, NOT NULL Int4/Int8/Text order columns, constant LIMIT, no OFFSET, no SRF. So every ORDER BY on tenk1/abbrev_abort_uuids materializes and sorts the whole table.

Line count: whole-block recount gives 555, not 830 (+50%): tuplesort 182 direct + 196 'current transaction is aborted' cascade = 378; join 61; limit 54 + 12 currval cascade = 66; memoize 18; tidscan 12; subselect 20. Only ~478 of them (tuplesort, limit, tidscan, join hunks 3404/5245/5293) are fixable by the budget alone.

Oracle facts wrong for 4 join statements (join.diff 8891-8912, oracle join.out 8027-8047): PostgreSQL expects `ERROR: column t1.uunique1 does not exist` + `HINT: Perhaps you meant to reference the column "t1.unique1"` (and the `ctid` ambiguity error), not rows. Gres runs the 50M-pair join before resolving the select list (build_from at exec.rs:19226/19255 precedes projection resolution) and has no column-name HINT at all (only the table-alias hint, session.rs:15072). Not a memory root; a bigger budget just makes them fail slower.

Comma-join WHERE->ON pushdown is all-or-nothing (exec.rs:13574-13585 append_from_item: the whole filter must resolve at that level and be an immutable_row_predicate). join.diff 2710 (`, tenk1 t4, tenk1 t5 where ...`) and subselect 727 (`tenk1 a, tenk1 b where a.thousand = b.thousand and exists(...)`) therefore run an unconstrained 10^8-pair cross join; no budget fixes that. Needs per-conjunct pushdown.

lateral_join (exec.rs:13595) receives no WHERE filter, so memoize's three statements (`LEFT JOIN LATERAL (...) ON TRUE WHERE s.c1 = s.c2 AND t1.unique1 < 1000`) loop 10000 outer x 10000 inner rows; the analyst attributes them to the budget but they need WHERE conjunct pushdown into the lateral loop.

100k-row join outputs (join 3585 `count(*) from tenk1 a, tenk1 b where a.hundred = b.thousand ...` = 100000; join 10886 OR-equijoin count; subselect 727) are 100k x 34 datums x ~100 B > 300 MB: no realistic budget fixes them. Gres's polymorphic_arguments_are_consistent already unifies these; the actual defect is routine.rs implicitly_coercible (1535) lacking int2->int4/int8/numeric/float8 and float4->float8, so `2::smallint` and `11::real` are refused. The dup(f1 anyelement, f2 out anyelement, f3 out anyarray) block (95 lines) is a parser cascade: parser.rs routine_arg (~14375) accepts `[mode] [name] type` but not PostgreSQL's `name mode type` order ('syntax error at position 43: expected RParen, found Ident("anyelement")'); the same gap breaks `create function dfunc(a variadic int[])` in polymorphism. The observed 'cannot change return type' on the later OR REPLACE is because a stray dup(anyelement) from collate.sql survived; not evidence for this root.

'RETURNS <table rowtype>' is already supported for public tables (routine.rs resolve_type 468 resolves relation names via RelationName::public); the failure 'type "users" does not exist' is because `users` is a TEMP table and resolve_type looks only in public. Fix is search_path/temp-schema resolution in resolve_type, not a new feature.

OUT-param result-type messages ('function result type must be integer because of OUT parameters') are CREATE-time checks in PostgreSQL; the fix belongs in build_routine (677) — normalise the result from OUT params and check the spelled RETURNS against it — not check_replaceable (875). The OR REPLACE failure today is RoutineResult::Unspecified != RoutineResult::Type when RETURNS is spelled on the replacement.

The Filter text ORDER is not 'policy quals then user quals': it follows PostgreSQL's order_qual_clauses (security level from contain_leaked_vars, then per-clause cost = procost*cpu_operator_cost, stable insertion sort). Oracle: `Filter: (f_leak(b) AND (a = 1))` (rls_sbv, f_leak COST 0.0000001 first), `Filter: (f_leak('abc'::text) AND ((a % 4) = 0) OR ...)` (Var-free non-leakproof qual gets level 0), `((a > 0) AND (a = 4) AND ((a % 2) = 0) AND f_leak(b))` (bv1), `((a <= 2) AND ((a % 2) = 0))` (EXECUTE p1). This needs a per-clause cost formula and built-in operator leakproof flags (routine cost/leakproof exist in pgcatalog routine.rs 262-263; nothing for built-in operators). 'Needs no cost model' is therefore only true for statistics, not for qual ordering.
